question: How do Vision Transformers scale with model size, data size and compute, and how can their training be made efficient enough to reach two billion parameters?
hypothesis: Scaling laws found for Transformer language models also hold for ViT transfer performance, with model, data and compute needing to grow together.
contributions: Characterisation of the performance-compute frontier for ViT on two datasets (JFT-3B, ImageNet-21k)
Improved large-scale training recipe: decoupled head weight decay, GAP/MAP head instead of [class] token, memory-efficient optimizers, infinite learning-rate schedules
ViT-G/14 (~2B parameters) reaching 90.45% ImageNet top-1 and 84.86% 10-shot

method.summary: Train ViTs from 5M to ~2B parameters on ImageNet-21k and JFT subsets up to 3B images for many step counts, and fit a saturating power law E=aC^-b+c (with shift d) of error against TPUv3 core-days. Along the way refine the recipe (head weight decay, MAP pooling, half-precision Adam/Adafactor, rsqrt schedule with cooldown) and train ViT-g/14 and ViT-G/14.
method.task: supervised image-classification pre-training, evaluated by few-shot linear transfer and full fine-tuning

datasets.name: JFT-3B
datasets.size: nearly 3 billion images, ~30k labels (29,593 classes in config); 927k near-duplicates removed
datasets.split: subsets of 30M, 300M, 1B, 3B images used for scaling
datasets.preprocessing: multi-label sigmoid cross-entropy; inception_crop(224), flip_lr; value_range(-1,1); duplicates of eval train/test images removed

datasets.name: ImageNet (ILSVRC-2012), ImageNet-v2, ReaL, ObjectNet
datasets.split: fine-tune on ImageNet; held-out 2% of train split used to pick fine-tune LR
datasets.preprocessing: eval: resize_small(256), central_crop(224) in pre-training config

datasets.name: VTAB-1k (19 tasks), Oxford-IIIT Pets, CIFAR-100, Caltech-UCSD Birds

models.name: ViT-G/14
models.architecture: ViT encoder, MAP head, no [class] token, no final non-linear projection

training.objective: multi-label sigmoid cross-entropy on JFT labels (hierarchy ignored)
training.optimizer: Adafactor modified: half-precision (bfloat16) first momentum, no relative-lr scaling, second momentum clipped at 0.999; beta1=0.9; grad clip norm 1.0
training.lr_schedule: reciprocal square-root (timescale 10000) with linear cooldown to zero (cooldown_steps 50000 in ViT-g config; 10K/50K in Tables 14-22)
training.batch_size: 4096 for models smaller than ViT-g; up to 32768 for ViT-g and ViT-G
training.steps: ViT-g config total_steps 1,000,000; tables report 20K to 6.3M steps (ViT-g/14) and 5M for ViT-G/14 (normalised to batch 4096)
training.precision: bfloat16 first momentum; second momentum in half precision degraded performance
training.weight_decay: head 3.0, body 0.03 (config: wd=0.03*8e-4, head kernel mult 100)
training.regularisation: very strong L2 on final linear layer only; inception crop, horizontal flip
training.hardware: TPUv3; ViT-g/ViT-G distributed over 2048 TPUv3 chips
training.compute: scaling study spans <1 to >10000 TPUv3 core-days (Fig 2 axis)
training.seeds: Table 1 reports +-; number of runs not stated

other.data_parallelism_only: whole ViT-G fits on a single TPUv3 core

other.few_shot: closed-form l2-regularised linear regression on frozen 224px embeddings
other.finetune: SGD with momentum, batch 512, grad clip global norm 1, no weight decay, 384px (models below ViT-g) or 518px (ViT-g, ViT-G), cosine schedule 20k steps (flat LR with Polyak averaging for ViT-G only), 500 warmup steps, LR swept {0.03, 0.01} on held-out 2% train split; VTAB: fixed LR 0.01, cosine, 2500 steps

metrics.name: n-shot ImageNet accuracy
metrics.definition: linear classifier on frozen features with n examples per class

eval.protocol: Pareto frontier over many (model, data, steps) runs; saturating power law fit; Table 1 shows mean +- value

limits: Pre-training data JFT-3B is proprietary; authors check laws on public ImageNet-21k (Limitations)
Conclusions 'may not necessarily generalize beyond the scale we have studied and they may not generalize beyond the ViT family'
Only ImageNet-style supervised classification pre-training; smaller models saturate at the lower end of compute so power law needs shift term
VTAB uses one hyperparameter; heavy per-task sweep (SOTA 79.99) left to future work
Pets few-shot fits do not match perfectly (Fig 9 caption)
Some rows missing in appendix Tables (authors say they do not affect trend)
Number of seeds behind +- in Table 1 not stated; no hyperparameter detail for ViT-G beyond ViT-g config listing

terms.definition: E = a(C+d)^-b + c: c is irreducible error at high compute, d shifts the x-axis because zero-compute models still get non-zero accuracy
